name: Krabi · Ao Nang & Railay
summary: Stay in Ao Nang for convenience or Railay for scenery; Railay is reached only by boat. Spend one day on the Hong or Four Islands and one on Railay's beaches and viewpoint.
seasonNote: May to October is monsoon: rough seas, cancelled boats and lower prices.
arrival: Krabi airport is 40 minutes from Ao Nang by shuttle or taxi; ferries link Phuket, Phi Phi and Koh Lanta.
gettingAround: Longtail boats from Ao Nang beach run to Railay when full; songthaews link Ao Nang and Krabi Town.
cashTip: Carry baht for boats, park fees and beach food; ATMs charge a fixed foreign-card fee.
foodTip: Try southern curries, grilled seafood, roti with banana and massaman curry.
buyTip: Batik and local snacks at Krabi Town's weekend walking street.
baseArea: Ao Nang for transport and price; Railay for the setting

connections.note: Seasonal ferries; about 3 hours by road.

items.name: Railay Beach
items.summary: A peninsula of white beaches walled in by limestone cliffs, reachable only by boat.
items.expect: Day-trip crowds from 10 am to 3 pm; monkeys take food.
items.tip: Go early by longtail and walk between West Railay, East Railay and Phra Nang.
items.why: It is the most beautiful beach setting on the mainland.
flow: Walk across to Phra Nang Cave Beach.

items.name: Phra Nang Cave Beach
items.summary: A cliff-backed beach with a shrine cave and climbers on the rock above.
items.expect: Longtail food boats and many visitors at midday.
items.tip: Arrive before 9 am; the steep viewpoint trail starts on the path from East Railay.
items.why: Often named among the world's best beaches.
flow: Walk the path from East Railay.
Swim, then see the Princess Cave shrine.

items.name: Hong Islands
items.summary: A group of islands with a hidden lagoon, a white beach and a 400-step viewpoint.
items.expect: A park fee on top of the tour price.
items.tip: Take a longtail rather than a speedboat for a calmer day.
items.why: The 360-degree viewpoint is the best island view in Krabi.
flow: Boat from Ao Nang or Klong Muang.
Lagoon, beach and the viewpoint staircase.

items.name: Tiger Cave Temple
items.summary: A temple at the foot of a cliff, with 1,260 steep steps to a golden Buddha on the summit.
items.expect: A very hard, hot climb; dress modestly.
items.tip: Start by 7 am and carry water.
items.why: The summit view over karst towers and the sea is superb.

items.name: Emerald Pool
items.summary: A clear green forest pool fed by warm springs, with a natural hot spring waterfall nearby.
items.expect: About an hour's drive; busy at weekends.
items.tip: Combine it with the Khlong Thom hot springs on one trip.
items.why: A refreshing jungle swim away from the coast.
flow: Walk the forest trail to the pool.
Soak in the hot spring cascade nearby.

items.name: Krabi Town Night Market
items.summary: A weekend walking street of food stalls, crafts and a stage.
items.expect: Friday to Sunday evenings only.
items.tip: Come hungry and share small plates.
items.why: The best cheap local food in the area.

items.name: Ao Nang seafood street
items.summary: A row of open-air seafood restaurants at the west end of the beach.
items.expect: Tourist prices; fish sold by weight.
items.tip: Confirm the price per 100 g before ordering.
items.why: Fresh fish with a sunset view.
flow: Walk the row and compare displays.
Choose a fish and how it is cooked.

items.name: Railay walking street
items.summary: A short lane of casual restaurants and bars behind West Railay beach.
items.expect: Simple food at island prices.
items.tip: Good for lunch between beaches.
items.why: The easiest place to eat on Railay without a resort bill.
flow: Order pad thai or a curry.

name: Koh Samui
tagline: Palm beaches in the Gulf of Thailand
summary: A resort island with an airport, good for a beach week. Chaweng is busy, Bophut and Maenam are calmer. Take a day boat to Ang Thong Marine Park, and a ferry on to Koh Phangan or Koh Tao.
seasonNote: The Gulf's rain comes October to December, the opposite of Phuket's season.
arrival: Fly direct to Samui (expensive), or fly to Surat Thani and take a bus and ferry (3 to 4 hours).
gettingAround: Songthaews circle the ring road; taxis rarely use meters, so agree the fare first.
cashTip: Carry baht for songthaews and markets.
foodTip: Try coconut-based southern curries, grilled seafood and fresh coconut ice cream.
buyTip: Coconut oil products and crafts at Fisherman's Village.
via: Via Bangkok, or Surat Thani plus ferry

connections.note: Direct flights; or via Surat Thani and ferry.

items.name: Ang Thong National Marine Park
items.wiki: Mu Ko Ang Thong National Park
items.summary: An archipelago of 42 jungle islands, with a green lagoon and a steep viewpoint.
items.expect: A full day by boat; closed roughly November to mid-December.
items.tip: Choose a tour that includes kayaking and the Koh Wua Talap viewpoint.
items.why: The islands that inspired 'The Beach'.
flow: Emerald Lake, kayak, then the viewpoint climb.

items.name: Wat Phra Yai (Big Buddha)
items.summary: A 12-metre golden seated Buddha on a small island joined by a causeway.
items.expect: Cover shoulders and knees.
items.tip: Pair it with Wat Plai Laem five minutes away.
items.why: The island's best-known landmark.

items.name: Wat Plai Laem
items.summary: A colourful lakeside temple with an 18-armed Guanyin statue.
items.expect: A short, photogenic stop.
items.tip: Buy fish food to feed the lake's catfish.
items.why: The most striking temple on Samui.
flow: Cross the walkways over the lake.
See the Guanyin and laughing Buddha.

items.name: Fisherman's Village, Bophut
items.summary: A beachfront street of old wooden Chinese shophouses, now cafés and boutiques.
items.expect: A big walking-street market on Friday evenings.
items.tip: Come on Friday night for the market.
items.why: The island's most charming place for an evening.
flow: Eat at a restaurant on the sand.

items.name: Na Muang Waterfalls
items.summary: Two purple-rock waterfalls in the jungle; the first has a swimming pool at its foot.
items.expect: A steep, slippery path to the second fall; avoid the elephant rides nearby.
items.tip: Best after rain; wear proper shoes.
items.why: A cool break from the beach.

items.name: Fisherman's Village Friday market
items.summary: A weekly night market with rows of street food and cocktail carts.
items.expect: Fridays from 5 pm; very crowded.
items.tip: Park outside the village and walk in.
items.why: The best street food evening on the island.

items.name: Lamai Night Plaza food stalls
items.summary: A nightly open-air food court in the centre of Lamai.
items.expect: Simple plastic tables.
items.tip: Cheaper than the beach restaurants.
items.why: Reliable, inexpensive Thai food every night.

items.name: Chaweng beachfront seafood
items.summary: Restaurants that set tables on the sand each evening and grill the day's catch.
items.expect: Tourist prices; fire shows after dark.
items.tip: Agree the price by weight first.
items.why: Dinner with your feet in the sand.

name: Ayutthaya
tagline: Ruins of the old Siamese capital
summary: The capital of Siam for 400 years until 1767, now brick temple ruins on a river island. It works as a day trip from Bangkok, but a night lets you see the temples lit and empty.
seasonNote: March to May is very hot; start at 8 am.
arrival: Trains from Bangkok take 60 to 90 minutes; minivans and tours take about the same.
gettingAround: Rent a bicycle or hire a tuk-tuk by the hour; the main ruins are a few kilometres apart.
cashTip: Temple tickets and tuk-tuks are cash only.
foodTip: Try boat noodles, grilled giant river prawns and roti sai mai (candy floss in a thin crêpe).
buyTip: Roti sai mai from the stalls near the hospital.
baseArea: On the island near the historical park
via: Via Bangkok, about 80 km by train or road

connections.note: Frequent trains from Krung Thep Aphiwat or Hua Lamphong.

items.name: Wat Mahathat
items.summary: A ruined monastery famous for a stone Buddha head held in the roots of a fig tree.
items.expect: A queue to photograph the head; crouch so you are lower than it.
items.tip: Visit first thing in the morning.
items.why: The most recognisable image of Ayutthaya.
flow: Find the Buddha head near the entrance.
Walk the rows of headless statues.

items.name: Wat Phra Si Sanphet
items.summary: Three bell-shaped chedis in a row, once the royal temple of the palace.
items.expect: Little shade.
items.tip: See the giant bronze Buddha at Wihan Phra Mongkhon Bophit next door.
items.why: It was the model for Bangkok's Temple of the Emerald Buddha.

items.name: Wat Chaiwatthanaram
items.summary: A Khmer-style riverside temple with a tall central tower ringed by smaller spires.
items.expect: Off the island; many visitors come in rented Thai costume.
items.tip: Come for sunset, when the brick glows.
items.why: The most photogenic ruin in the city.

items.name: Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon
items.summary: A working monastery with a huge climbable chedi and rows of saffron-draped Buddhas.
items.expect: Busy with Thai worshippers.
items.tip: Climb the chedi for a view over the grounds.
items.why: It shows how the ruins looked when they were in use.

items.name: Bang Pa-In Royal Palace
items.summary: A summer palace of Thai, Chinese and European pavilions around ornamental lakes.
items.expect: Strict dress code; 20 km south of the city.
items.tip: Stop on the way to or from Bangkok.
items.why: A complete contrast to the ruins: manicured and intact.
flow: Rent a golf cart or walk.
See the pavilion in the lake and the Chinese-style mansion.

items.name: Boat noodle shops by Wat Mahathat
items.summary: Small shops serving tiny bowls of dark, rich noodle soup, once sold from canal boats.
items.expect: Bowls are small; order several.
items.tip: Stack your bowls and count them at the end.
items.why: Ayutthaya is the home of boat noodles.

items.name: Riverside grilled river prawns
items.summary: Riverside restaurants grilling giant freshwater prawns over charcoal.
items.expect: Priced by weight and not cheap.
items.tip: Ask the price per kilo; mix the head fat with rice.
items.why: The city's signature splurge for Thai visitors.
flow: Order prawns by weight with seafood sauce.

items.name: Roti sai mai stalls
items.summary: A strip of stalls selling coloured sugar floss to wrap in thin roti.
items.expect: Takeaway bags; very sweet.
items.tip: Buy a small bag and roll them yourself.
items.why: The sweet Ayutthaya is known for across Thailand.
flow: Pick a stall making it fresh.
Roll the floss in a roti.

name: Chiang Rai
tagline: The White Temple and the far north
summary: A quiet northern city known for three modern art temples: white, blue and black. Many visit on a long day trip from Chiang Mai, but two nights lets you add the Golden Triangle and tea hills.
seasonNote: March and April bring heavy smoke haze; rain falls June to October.
arrival: Three hours by bus from Chiang Mai; the airport has flights from Bangkok.
gettingAround: Hire a driver or scooter for the temples, which are spread out; the centre is walkable.
cashTip: Carry baht for temples and markets.
foodTip: Try khao soi, nam ngiao (tomato and pork noodle soup) and sai ua northern sausage.
buyTip: Hill-tribe textiles and local tea and coffee from Doi Chang and Doi Mae Salong.
baseArea: Near the clock tower and night bazaar

connections.note: Frequent buses; book ahead at weekends.

items.name: Wat Rong Khun (White Temple)
items.summary: A dazzling white and mirrored temple by artist Chalermchai Kositpipat, part shrine, part art project.
items.expect: One-way route with tour groups from 10 am; no photos inside the hall.
items.tip: Arrive at opening, 8 am.
items.why: There is nothing else like it in Thailand.
flow: Cross the bridge over the sea of hands.
See the murals, then the golden building.

items.name: Wat Rong Suea Ten (Blue Temple)
items.summary: A sapphire-blue and gold temple with a white seated Buddha inside.
items.expect: Small and free; busy midday.
items.tip: Try the blue coconut ice cream at the gate.
items.why: Its colour is extraordinary in late light.

items.name: Baan Dam Museum (Black House)
items.summary: About 40 dark wooden buildings filled with horns, skins and carved furniture by artist Thawan Duchanee.
items.expect: Dark and unsettling to some; closed for lunch.
items.tip: See it as the counterpart to the White Temple.
items.why: A singular artist's vision of death and desire.
flow: Wander the smaller houses in the garden.

items.name: Golden Triangle
items.summary: The meeting point of Thailand, Laos and Myanmar on the Mekong, with an excellent opium museum.
items.expect: A long drive and a touristy riverfront.
items.tip: The Hall of Opium is the real reason to go.
items.why: A place with a notorious history, well explained.
flow: See the viewpoint, then the Hall of Opium.

items.name: Chiang Rai Clock Tower
items.summary: A golden clock tower by the White Temple's artist, with a light and music show each evening.
items.expect: Shows on the hour at 7, 8 and 9 pm.
items.tip: Watch from a café on the corner.
items.why: A quick, free evening sight.

items.name: Chiang Rai Night Bazaar
items.summary: A nightly market with a large food court, hotpots and a stage of local music.
items.expect: Lively but relaxed.
items.tip: Try the clay-pot hotpot at the yellow tables.
items.why: Dinner and souvenir shopping in one place.
flow: Eat in the food court by the stage.

items.name: Lung Eed Locol Food
items.summary: A simple shop known for northern-style laap with crisp chicken skin.
items.expect: Lunch only; basic seating.
items.tip: Order the chicken laap with sticky rice.
items.why: A local favourite for a northern classic.
flow: Order laap gai and sticky rice.

items.name: Chivit Thamma Da
items.summary: A riverside colonial-style house serving coffee, cakes and Thai and Western dishes.
items.expect: Higher prices than town.
items.tip: Walk here from the Blue Temple.
items.why: The prettiest place in the city for a long lunch.
flow: Take a garden table by the river.
Order coffee and cake or a northern set.

name: Koh Phi Phi
summary: A car-free island between Phuket and Krabi. Stay a night or two to see Maya Bay and the viewpoint before and after the day boats. Tonsai village is loud at night; the east coast is quiet.
seasonNote: May to October brings rough crossings; Maya Bay closes for about two months in low season.
arrival: Ferries from Phuket and Krabi take 90 minutes to 2 hours.
gettingAround: Walk in the village; longtail boats reach other beaches.
cashTip: Carry baht; there is an arrival fee at the pier and ATMs can run dry.
foodTip: Grilled seafood, Thai curries and fruit shakes; prices are higher than the mainland.
buyTip: Little worth buying; bring reef-safe sunscreen with you.
baseArea: Tonsai edge for convenience; Long Beach or Laem Tong for quiet

connections.note: To Krabi's Klong Jilad pier or Ao Nang.

items.name: Maya Bay
items.summary: A cove enclosed by 100-metre cliffs, made famous by the film 'The Beach'.
items.expect: No swimming; timed visits, a park fee, and closed around August and September.
items.tip: Take a 7 am longtail to arrive before the Phuket speedboats.
items.why: Still one of the most beautiful bays in Asia, and blacktip sharks have returned.
flow: Longtail to the rear pier at Loh Samah.
Walk the boardwalk to the beach.

items.name: Phi Phi Viewpoint
items.summary: A hilltop view over the twin bays and the narrow sand strip between them.
items.expect: A steep 25-minute climb with a small fee.
items.tip: Go for sunrise or late afternoon.
items.why: The classic photograph of the island.
flow: Climb the steps from the village.

items.name: Pileh Lagoon
items.summary: An emerald lagoon between vertical cliffs where boats stop for swimming.
items.expect: Many boats by mid-morning.
items.tip: Visit on the same early trip as Maya Bay.
items.why: The best swimming stop around the islands.
flow: Enter by longtail at high tide.

items.name: Bamboo Island
items.summary: A small flat island ringed by white sand and shallow reef.
items.expect: A national park fee.
items.tip: Combine with Mosquito Island for snorkelling.
items.why: The best beach in the group.

items.name: Long Beach
items.summary: A quieter stretch of sand with a view of Phi Phi Leh, 10 minutes by longtail from Tonsai.
items.expect: Fewer facilities.
items.tip: Walk the coastal path at low tide or take a boat.
items.why: The best swimming beach near the village.
flow: Swim and snorkel off the south end.

items.name: Tonsai village market stalls
items.summary: A small local market in the village lanes with cheap Thai dishes and fruit.
items.expect: Basic stalls.
items.tip: The cheapest meals on the island.
items.why: Good Thai food at near-mainland prices.
flow: Find the market behind the pier.

items.name: Loh Dalum beachfront grills
items.summary: Beach restaurants that grill seafood at dusk before the fire shows start.
items.expect: Loud music later at night.
items.tip: Eat early, then leave or stay for the fire show.
items.why: Sunset dinner on the sand.

items.name: Garlic 1992
items.summary: A long-running family restaurant for Thai dishes at fair prices.
items.expect: A queue at dinner.
items.tip: Go early or late.
items.why: The village's most dependable Thai food.
flow: Order massaman curry and stir-fried morning glory.
